answer: Because the declaration is checked against funding history rather than taken on trust, the island registry records each claim and the harbor audit publishes every slash. A farm must therefore either lie, which the cedar graph proves on replay, or recruit 173 outsiders whose stake is exposed alongside its own. Attesters sign a declaration that they hold no common funding with the identity they attest, and a later finding of common funding voids the attestation and slashes 65% of the attester's bond. That is 8 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
